Silent Hill 2 is simply one of the greatest horror games ever made. What makes it so special to me is how much of the fear comes from inside, not outside. The monsters, the fog, the town itself — everything feels like a reflection of James’s mind, his guilt, his grief, his need for punishment. It’s not just about being scared, it’s about being unsettled all the way down, and that’s what makes it unforgettable.  I love how everything in the game means something. Pyramid Head isn’t just a monster, he’s James’s guilt given form. The environments aren’t just creepy, they feel like memories rotting away. Even the other characters you meet feel like echoes of trauma, each carrying their own despair. It’s all so layered, and the more you think about it, the darker it gets.  The story is devastating. James isn’t some action hero — he’s broken, and as the truth unravels you realize just how tragic it all is. It’s rare for a game to make you feel horror and heartbreak at the same time, but Silent Hill 2 does it better than anything else I’ve played. The atmosphere, the pacing, the sound design, Akira Yamaoka’s music — every piece comes together perfectly.  It’s clunky sometimes, sure, especially the combat, but honestly I don’t even care. The awkwardness just makes the game feel heavier, slower, more suffocating. It’s part of the experience.  Silent Hill 2 isn’t just a horror game. It’s a masterpiece about grief, guilt, memory, and how far people will go to hide from or face the truth. It’s stuck with me more than any other horror game ever has, and probably always will.  Thanks Team Silent! :)

An outstanding game. A faithful yet innovative remake of the original 2001 title.   This game is haunting, melancholic, and thought-provoking. The themes were nailed perfectly here; it is a clear project of passion and appreciation for the original material. Every bit screams that it was hand-crafted intentionally, every detail well thought out and designed with purpose, both during gameplay, cutscenes, and even in menus. This remake features a surprisingly impressive range of accessibility customisation. I cannot state enough how massively appreciated Bloober Team's careful thought to implement every one of these options is. More on this later.  This game offers a special experience within the survival-horror genre due to its especially rich storytelling. I admire Silent Hill 2 for its thoughtful attention to detail, symbolism, and the way the environments tell the story more often than things being spoken outright. I devoured this game for the way it let me sink into it and become a part of the world, carefully dissecting each piece of it and pondering its meaning. Some things were surely more obvious than others, but I loved its constant invitation to *dig*.   Silent Hill 2 is stunning and immersive in both exploration and cinematics. Across the board, the vocal performances, animations, etc were completely spot-on decisions. If some award is not won for this, I'll honestly be shocked.  The combat isn't a particularly stand-out feature, lacking specialty and depth, but those aspects of the game are not intended to be the focus, and frankly never have been. Atmosphere and narrative have always been the focus of Silent Hill, and what makes the series so memorable and iconic to this very day. The original game was formatted in a way that required the player to control James from an almost birds-eye angle, the camera being fixed in one corner of the room. This lead to somewhat wonky controls, and makes for iconic yet frustrating gunplay in retrospect. Somewhat drawing from this, the Silent Hill 2 remake features equally "vanilla" gunplay, without bells and whistles that overcomplicate things without reason. The guns are slightly inaccurate seemingly regardless of how you attempt to handle them, but perhaps this was entirely intentional. Is James an experienced gun wielder, or is he just desperately attempting to fend off these walking nightmares?  I spent a big portion of the beginning of my play-through chuckling away as I charged about Silent Hill, smashing car windows and breaking into stores, as well as repeatedly stomping enemies' bodies after they'd jumps-cared me. This game was immense fun from start to finish, all while being perfectly disturbing, tense, and heartbreaking when it should have been.  But this enjoyment was not without some frustration.  I played on Medium settings, with certain features set to "off" where possible; a routine setup for my system regardless of the game.   Originally the iconic fog that has settled over Silent Hill didn't exist solely to create atmosphere, rather was a clever strategy to assist the original system - the PlayStation One -  in rendering nearby surroundings, and eliminate the need to focus on anything too far away. It was a smart benefit to the system at the time, yet now it's ironically a resource hog. The mist itself is not a solid block as it used to be, now causing frames to drop because of particle effects. I couldn't help but find this slightly comedic, given the original design purpose.   Despite my PC being well within (actually above) the recommended specifications, I try to eliminate as much as possible to allow for some breathing room whilst still maintaining visual quality. Unfortunately, despite my attempts to optimise the game, I suffered consistent frame-drops and stuttering from start to finish.   I was forced to lower the difficulty of combat because on many occasions I either died or wasted ammunition due to the performance issues. It did remove a layer of intensity on numerous occasions, as the briefly frozen frames provided a crack through the immersion so I could recover or react to whatever may have been going on at times.  Accessibility is something that I am deeply passionate about. I advocate for as much accessibility in gaming as possible wherever I can. I have made numerous complaints across different games regarding the inability to customise features to suit one's preferences or to assist one's disability. Games should be fun to experience, first and foremost. I wholeheartedly believe that everyone deserves a fair shot at something they aim to achieve if it's realistically within reach and they have the drive to do so.  Silent Hill 2 remake well and truly blew me away as one of the most inclusive and carefully considered games I've played personally. I cannot quite articulate how thrilled I was. It was truly something special to browse the menu and feel cared for, something myself and many others experience all to little of within gaming. Bloober Team's systems allowed customisation of a wide range of settings.   These included (but were not at all limited to):  HUD - Reticle Visibility (Off/Minimal/Dynamic - displays a range of reticle shapes and designs for various weapons) - Reticle Thickness (Thin/Normal/Thick - made the actual lines of the gun's reticle bolder and thus more apparent) - Reticle opacity (Slider - self-explanatory) - Low Health Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are coloured when James is injured) - Splatter Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are splattered when James is attacked)  INTERACTIONS - Interaction Icon Visibility (Off/Icon/Button Icon - choice of display type for interactable items, display just a dot or the button required to interact) - Interaction Icon Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - displays the previous setting much smaller or larger than default for easy spotting)  GRAPHICS - Colourblind Mode (Normal vision/Deuteranope/Protanope/Tritanope - self-explanatory) - Colourblind Mode Severity (Slider - changes vibrancy of colour-altered effects) - High Contrast Mode (Off/On - makes all scenery monochromatic grey, completely recolouring allies, enemies, environmental interactables, save points, and James himself for visibility. When "on", able to select White/Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Red/Green/Blue for each individual specified model.)  AUDIO  - Night Mode (Off/On - dampens the effect of typical loud sounds like "bang"s)  TEXTS  - Non-Verbal Captions Visibility (Off/On - things like *gate creaks*, and notable ambient sounds captioned) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size Font (Default/Bold/Dyslexic - self-explanatory.) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - self-explanatory) - Subtitle Names (Off/On - tells you who the speaker is in subtitled-text)  Each of these settings are located where you'd expect to find them depending on topic, however there is an additional screen entitled ACCESSIBILITY where it compiles all of these settings into one place for easy-access. It blew my mind that this game had so many options including a dedicated font for dyslexia. I nearly cried. I have OpenDyslexic font installed on my browser so that I can easily digest long strings of information when surfing the web. I never thought I'd actually see it implemented in a video-game.   I purchased the game from an external retailer, but on Steam, this title currently stands at $102.50 AUD. I'm uncertain if that's the same or much lower than what I paid upon release, but I believe it's reasonable for the overall fantastic experience this game provided.

A fully fleshed out game (pun intended). It can be hard to justify $70, but this game was truly an extended, immersive experience.   Pros: -The level of detail and the graphics are INSANE. The characters are much more realistic. (when i heard it was "woke" i knew it was gonna be good). From pictures/screenshots it may seem like the characters look odd, but when you're actually in the game & interacting with them: its much more realistic, emotive, detailed, and it all makes sense. It gives "Monster House" for adults vibes. -New endings -New puzzles -It honored not only the original Silent Hill 2 game- but also the original and all of the games by Team Silent. -More immersion into the world -The combat is MUCH smoother -This game fills in a lot of the gaps in the original SH2. You still have to infer things, and its still FILLED with metaphors: but everything is more fully fleshed out. I do think it aligns with what the original idea that Team Silent had, back when they made it. But back in the day: PS2 games were rarely this long. So you had to draw a lot of conclusions yourself, or look up theories. I like that this was a fully-told, hauntingly-beautiful, story. -There is no such thing as "Easy" mode. There is a "Light" mode, which is still extremely challenging & difficult to do. I dont know if this is a pro, or a con, but I know a lot of gamers like to be challenged: so im including it with the pros.  Cons: -There is a bug during the Xray puzzle: where the x-rays that were initially on the wall: disappear when you come back, after collecting the missing x-ray. To fix this: go save your game, reload it, and all of the photos should be there when you load it up again. -Some items just cannot be picked up. This didnt affect gameplay or success though. -Some small visual bugs like guns not physically appearing in hands, but you can still shoot them -The voices were really hard to hear over the sound effects. I wish there was a way to turn that up, without having explosive audio shortly afterwards. -Some of the puzzles, even on light mode: are nearly impossible without a guide. There are just no hints at all for some of the puzzles, and you basically just have to figure it out. So you would be there for many hours. -Silent Hill loves a good prison segment, honey. And of course the prison portion of this game is the most maddening & the worst.

Just finished this.   I gotta be honest with you, I think I was expecting more from a name as legendary in the gaming industry as Silent Hill 2.  Before playing, I was excited to finally be able to play Silent Hill 2 after hearing about it for literal decades. Frequently said to be the scariest game ever made, and the story regularly praised to the moon and back.  After playing, I was just kind of relieved that I was just over and done with the game. The game just feels far too bloated for how basic the gameplay is.  While I appreciated a lot of what the game has to offer, I did like the puzzles, the gameplay does feel draining after a while since there is literally only like 4 enemies in the game you'll be fighting against. See one of the basic enemies? Hit it with a pipe and dodge away before it blows up. Puppets? Beat the shit out of them with your pipe. Nurses? Beat the shit out of them with our pipe and occasionally gun them down if you don't feel like dealing with them. Repeat 15+ hours. The solution is every encounter is beating the shit out of everything with your pipe. It doesn't feel like an issue in the first half though, but you'll definitely feel the lack of gameplay variety as the game goes on. I was really feeling it by the time I reached the prison, and that's about 3/5 through the game. On top of that, Silent Hill 2 never really felt scary to me. I can name maybe 3 instances in the entire game where I was a little spooked. Tense and creepy? Yes. Scary? Rarely. Silent Hill 2 is probably a little bit scarier than RE4 Remake, less scary than Dead Space Remake. But that's coming from a major fan of Resident Evil 7, RE8's House Beneviento section, Outlast and Alien Isolation, so of course my expectations were gonna be high when it comes to scare factor.   Don't get me wrong, Silent Hill 2 has a lot of cool moments. The first half is excellent. Extremely dreadful, extremely tense, always masterfully pulling you along and asking yourself what is going to happen next, and how James's story is going to be slowly unravelled. The environments are incredibly detailed, atmosphere is harrowing as hell, the process of figuring out puzzles is really fun, music is haunting (but occasionally cheesy), exploration and level design is fun, boss fights are fun (except maybe the last two boss fights). Unfortunately, most of the game's narrative feels like an illogical carrot on a string. It unravels itself, yes, but it doesn't ever really give you a satisfying climax in the way I was expecting. It just stays in this wierd, vague, mysterious, ambiguous, nightmarish limbo that the rest of the story was submerged in. Always teasing you with something more, and barely delivering, letting the human mind fill the gaps. But I guess that's just the draw for Silent Hill. Everything is illogical. Even the enemy designs are that way. Things in Silent Hill are rarely explained, and when something IS explained, it's generally extremely vague, just enough to give you an idea of what is going on in this twisted and foggy town. Personally, I prefer something a little more blunt, storytelling wise.  I will say that I commend Luke Roberts's voice acting performance. He did a fantastic job. I will also say that Bloober Team has made a pretty good game here, against all odds. Before, Bloober has made incredibly mediocre games, so of course people were expecting this game to be mediocre as well. Bloober proved the doubters wrong. Silent Hill 2 Remake proves that Bloober has the talent to make something genuinely good.  I enjoyed this game, (I LOOOOVED this one section with Angela in particular) I just hope that Bloober continually improves themselves and learns from their experience with this game so we can get something truly incredible from them in the future, I think it'll be a while before that happens though.  8/10

Alors oui c'est beau, mais mon dieu j'ai rarement vu un jeu si cher aussi mal optimisé. Le pauvre stagiaire qui a bourré cette partie là et c'est toujours pas corrigé..........  Deuxièmement, le gameplay des combats... nuuul... j'ai l'impression de revenir sur un vieux jeu de PS1, lent, limité, et la maniabilité d'un tank bourré... bon OK, l'original est sur PS2, mais ils auraient pu faire un effort sur le gameplay.  La difficulté change un seul paramètre : la barre de vie des ennemis qui se transforme en sac à PV. OK, bon point, on peut rendre les ennemis nul en mode facile ce qui est pas trop mal et rajoute à l'ambiance.  Pour ce qui est du reste, c'est-à-dire de le vivre comme un walking simulator, avec une histoire, et quelques ennemis qui rajoute à l'ambiance. Wow, quelle claque. la D.A. incroyable, l'ambiance, tortueuse, labyrinthique, l'histoire qui a un vrai sens, dans lequel on ressent des choses avec les personnages. Franchement, du grand art. Sans les problèmes un peu chiant du dessus ça aurait été un 10/10 pour moi.  Sacré expérience à vivre, peut-être la seul chose à dire c'est que c'est vraiment *putain* de violent et infernal. Serrez votre ceinture.

As a long time fan of the Silent Hill series, I was so excited to see one of the OGs getting a proper remake!! I played the original many years ago when i was very young, but never fully finished it until around the time this game came out last year. (I was very young and couldn't figure out tank controls lol). The original is nothing short of amazing, but guys lets face it, its showing its age.   That though, is where this game shines. Bloober absolutely nailed it. The story is still just as incredible as we remember, but the updated gameplay and visuals make it a lotttt easier to actually play and enjoy. The slightly updated soundtrack is great!! So glad they brought back Akira for it :) You probably have heard online from some that this game blows, because some people cant move past their nostalgic, rose colored glasses, but I can tell you right now, that this game is opposite of that. The OG will always, ALWAYS be a classic, and regarded as one of the best horror games, but this new take to the game brings extra depth that we didn't know we needed.   Let's talk about the acting.....HELLOOOOO ITS PHENOMENAL?? Luke Roberts as James, Salome Gunnarsdottir as Mary/Maria, Gianna Kiehl as Angela, Scott Haining and Danny Kirrane as Eddie, and Evie Templeton as Laura all brought a fresh, emotional weight to these already great characters with tragic backstories. Once again, you will hear a lot say that these folk weren't as good as the original cast....hate to break it to everyone but they're better. The budget was higher in 2024 and in return we got professional actors. Their performances elevated the story to a new level.   This remake gives the OG a second life, and it brought so many new fans to the series! It honors the original while bringing in some new things. I cant wait to see SH1 remake and SHf, but also any other Bloober projects!

Silent Hill 2 2024 — это поистине шедевр современного игрового искусства, который вновь поднимает планку в жанре психологического хоррора и оставляет незабываемое впечатление на всех, кто вступает в его мрачный и загадочный мир.  От первых минут погружения в игру чувствуешь особую атмосферу: тоскливое, зловещее настроение, пропитанное ощущением внутренней борьбы и невидимой опасности. Разработчики мастерски смогли сохранить дух легендарной серии, одновременно внедрив новые технологии, графику и драматургию, что делает Silent Hill 2 2024 по-настоящему современным и актуальным.  Графика впечатляет — каждый уголок города пропитан мраком и загадками. Детали окружения проработаны до мелочей: размытые тени, переливы света и тьмы, жуткая атмосфера, создающая ощущение постоянной тревоги и непредсказуемости. Всё это усиливает эффект погружения и заставляет сердце биться чаще.  Герой, которого мы ведём, — яркий пример удачного баланса: сильный, уязвимый одновременно, со своей историей и внутренней болью. Диалоги и его внутренняя борьба раскрывают глубокие психоэмоциональные нюансы, делая каждого игрока частью этого психологического триллера.  Музыкальное сопровождение — отдельное произведение искусства, идеально дополняющее всю атмосферу: haunting melodies, unsettling ambient sounds и тихие ноты, вызывающие целую гамму эмоций — от тревоги до сочувствия.  Геймплей в Silent Hill 2 2024 — это не только исследование жутких локаций и решение головоломок, это погружение в психологическую драму, где каждое решение и каждое звуко- и зрительное впечатление влияют на восприятие истории.  Silent Hill 2 2024 — это истинное произведение искусства, которое заслуженно занимает место в сердцах фанатов и новых игроков. Итог — игра великолепна, неподдельна и наполнена духом оригинальной серии, при этом свежа и актуальна. Обязательна к прохождению всем любителям хоррора и психологического драматизма.

The game does have optimization issues, but with some tweaking you can find a good balance between performance and visuals. That said, the game itself is just fantastic. It delivers everything the original did, and in some aspects it even surpasses it. The atmosphere, sound design, graphics, and narrative are all spot-on. If you played the original, you might not feel the same level of fear or anxiety you once did, but this remake will absolutely leave you with the sense that you’ve once again experienced a true Silent Hill game. Huge thanks to Bloober Team for giving me the chance to relive one of my favorite games of all time.

📝 English review below / Reseña en inglés más abajo  ⸻  🔶 El terror más profundo no viene de afuera, viene de adentro.  ⸻  📝 RESEÑA EN ESPAÑOL  Voy a contar un poco mi historia con este juego. La primera vez que lo jugué fue en la década de los 2000, cuando todavía no llegaba a los 15 años. No logré pasar ni un tercio porque me daba demasiado miedo, así que terminé abandonándolo.  Hoy, muchos años después, me doy cuenta de algo más fuerte: no solo no lo iba a terminar, sino que tampoco lo iba a entender. Este Silent Hill no se limita a dar miedo con monstruos o escenarios oscuros, sino que toca el verdadero terror: el que genera nuestra propia mente. Habla de traumas, de culpas, de rencores… y nos muestra que la batalla más grande es contra nosotros mismos.  Como decía Carl Jung con el concepto de la sombra, este juego nos enfrenta con esa parte oscura de nuestra psique que escondemos por miedo. En ese sentido, Silent Hill 2 Remake es tan realista como perturbador: no se trata solo de sobrevivir, sino de mirarnos en un espejo incómodo.  Lo recomiendo a quienes estén preparados para algo más que un survival horror. Porque puede ayudarnos a ser más sinceros con nosotros mismos y, en consecuencia, también con los demás.  ⸻  ✅ Puntos positivos: • Una historia profunda y psicológica. • Terror que trasciende lo superficial. • Personajes y atmósfera que dejan huella. • Excelente reinterpretación en el remake.  ❌ Puntos negativos: • No es para cualquiera: puede ser demasiado perturbador. • Jugabilidad que en algunos momentos se siente pesada. • Exige estar en el “estado mental” correcto para apreciarlo.  ⸻  🎯 Conclusión:  Más que un juego de terror, es un viaje a lo más oscuro de la mente humana. Silent Hill 2 Remake no solo asusta: confronta, incomoda y deja pensando. Una experiencia única para quienes se animen a mirarse dentro.  🔸 PUNTUACIÓN FINAL: 9/10 El miedo más real es el que llevamos dentro.  ⸻  📝 REVIEW IN ENGLISH  🔶 The deepest fear doesn’t come from the outside — it comes from within.  ⸻  Let me share a bit of my story with this game. The first time I played it was back in the 2000s, when I was under 15 years old. I couldn’t get past even a third of the game because it scared me so much, so I abandoned it.  Today, looking back as an adult, I realize something bigger: not only was I not going to finish it, I wasn’t even going to understand it. This Silent Hill doesn’t just scare with monsters or dark environments — it dives into the fear created by our own minds. It’s about trauma, guilt, resentment… and it shows us that the greatest battle is against ourselves.  As Carl Jung described with the concept of the shadow, this game confronts us with the darkest part of our psyche that we hide out of fear. In that sense, Silent Hill 2 Remake is as realistic as it is disturbing: it’s not just about surviving, it’s about facing an uncomfortable reflection.  I recommend it to those who are ready for something deeper than a survival horror. It can genuinely help us treat ourselves — and others — more sincerely.  ⸻  ✅ Pros: • Deep, psychological storytelling. • Fear that goes beyond the superficial. • Memorable characters and atmosphere. • Strong reinterpretation in the remake.  ❌ Cons: • Not for everyone: can be too disturbing. • Gameplay can feel heavy at times. • Requires the right mental state to fully appreciate.  ⸻  🎯 Conclusion:  More than a horror game, it’s a journey into the darkest corners of the human mind. Silent Hill 2 Remake doesn’t just scare — it confronts, unsettles, and lingers. A unique experience for those brave enough to look within.  🔸 FINAL SCORE: 9/10 The scariest fear is the one we carry inside.

it's the remake for probably the best psychological horror game of all time, the stakes were high, the source content is videogame art and the pressure on Bloober i bet was difficult to deal with.  So, how did it go? well they did a great job, it's not perfect but it could have been a lot worse, imo it's worthy of carrying such name but I feel like it could have been a little more better, the only cons I can think of are the following.   - Character designs, I don't know but Mary/Maria  to me is a huge downgrade compared to the one on the original game, Angela is a little more of the same, although I did not like the original Angela that much, the new one looks weird, James is a bit hit or miss for me, Eddy and Laura are the ones that look like the most like the ones on the og game.  - Too many manequins every corner, I feel like they did to much combat on this one specially on some areas, like outside Brooksheaven Hospital, I know you could avoid them but they becoming such a common occurence makes the tension fall off a little bit.  - UE5 I know UE5 allow devs to get cinematic looking graphics easier and quicker, but the tradeoff is bot Image quality (ironic) and performance, I played with a 5800x3d and a 3080 some things look extremely cool but the noisy shadows and reflections sometimes killed the vibe, also I had to use DLSS Balanced to get decent framerates at 1440p, another issue is the occasional traversal stutter that occur on designated places, this game as 90% UE5 games is very infuriating cause you can see how great it could have been if Epic fixed their engine and devs gave a f about IQ and performance.

What can I say? I have never played a Silent Hill game. One of my friends has always told me its a great game, so I decided to try it out. Wishing I would have never even heard it was on PC because I could have saved myself 70 dollars. Sadly I purchased the game from G2A so I cant even ask for a refund from Steam. My fault for avoiding paying full price I guess... but worked out in the end because I would have been furious if I paid 100 dollars for this game. Where to begin....Performance. Frame rate is not an issue for me. I have absolutely no issue running this game MAX graphics with RT on with a stable 60 FPS. Its the absolutely absurd traversal micro stutter that is the issue here. It does not matter if my graphics are set to ALL LOW, it stutters in the same exact spots, every time. Even if you run through the whole level and try to properly build the shader cache. 80% OF THE GAME YOU CANT SEE 30 FEET IN FRONT OF YOU, BUT IM LAGGING WHILE RUNNING? Explain to me how I can run any game, High graphics, DLSS quality at 2k with 100+ fps with ZERO ISSUES, but I cant run this game on the lowest settings. THE ONLY work around for me is using NVIDIA rec. settings from the NVIDIA App (which is essentially medium settings), turn shadows to low (from suggestions via online research) then running 1080p with DLSS on performance. It doesnt look terrible, but its absolutely unacceptable. When I can play RDR2 with no issues, or Forza Horizon 5, Spider Man Remastered (also a notoriously bad PC port) and any other new game without any issues, something is wrong here. Alas, here we are in 2025. The game still hasn't been optimized properly, and they have released another game entirely without even fixing the broken one. They suggest to run the game at 30fps to avoid the stuttering.....guess what? you can literally still see the slow downs at 30 FPS. I have tried mods, fixes, DLSS swapper, capping frame rate to 30,40,50,60,75 and 90. Nothing works, the community gaslights you into believing the game isn't poorly optimized and that for some reason half the world cant build a PC properly. Ok. Bye, Felicia. In what may be a surprise to some, Bloober has accomplished what no other western dev (except maybe Sam Barlow) has done before and made a Silent Hill entry that matches the quality the original trilogy had. I had no doubts, judging from past experience on The Medium (a bit of a Polish take on Silent Hill, with an understandably questionable ending). Pros: the atmosphere and tone matches the original perfectly. Both games are what I call oppressively dark. Some may find it hard to play in long stretches, but that is part of the charm. The biggest surprise has to be the quality of all acting performances. Angela is probably my most favorite nuanced performance. Yamaokas soundtrack is still awesome and the sound design is still unsettling.  Cons: UE5 stutter strikes once again. Performance could be more optimized. I did not bother with turning on raytracing, not that I wanted it (would be nice with some darker levels) but because frame pacing is bad enough even without it. There is too much combat in this remake, with a combat system that is deliberately clumsy since James is a depressed dude. Problems come up with hit tracking. Many times he will just whiff or swings will pass through monsters.  Overall, this game is a must play for anyone with any interest in the godfather of psychological horror games. Hopefully Bloober is working on the Born From a Wish dlc. Very much looking forward to Silent Hill f.

Does it suck? No. Does it blow the original out of the water? Also no. SH2 offers a solid modernized take the revolutionary classic.   I think it found a way to implement the "modern third-person shooter" mechanics and keeping them tight and functional, without taking away from making James feel like a normal dude on mission rather than a Special Forces officer. Graphically, the look of the town has never looked better. I liked the new scenes. There's only few enough that it adds flavor without feeling tacked on, and aside the them, the original dialogue 99% intact. The bosses are definitely a lot more intense if you played on hard difficulty. Puzzles are a lot easier, even on Hard, so make of that what you will.  My main gripes are mild ones, mostly with some of the sound design. Some of the musical cues don't match up at all with the original, and some of the voice acting left a bit to be desired. It's not like how SH2 2001 had awkward reads that gave it Lynch-esque surreality, just flatness that can take you out of the experience sometimes.  Had a lot of fun, though. Will definitely 100% and look forward to the SH1 remake.

Ganz ehrlich ich wollte einfach nur das es vorbei ist, das einzige was an ein Remake rankommt war der Prolog und das Hotel, die dann aber auch wirklich gut waren und Spaß gemacht haben, der Rest war wirklich nicht gut. Es ist okay für ein Remake ein neues Kampfsystem einzuführen, aber dann mach es richtig oder gar nicht, aber nicht diese kacke. Warum brauchte man zwingend einen Dodge? Hätte man den Dodge eingebaut und dann sowas wie eine Heavy und Light Attack eingebaut hätte könnte es vlt angenehm sein, aber man hat leider nur Schlagen oder nicht Schlagen und im Remake sind praktisch alle Gegner encounter Pflicht, man hat, nicht wie im Original, keine Möglichkeiten denen auszuweichen. Die Gegner folgen dir durch Türen, haben sehr unvorhersehbare Geschwindigkeiten, da sie für einen Angriff auch gerne zum Spieler teleportieren und Tauchen manchmal aus dem nichts auf, ohne dass das Radio ausschlägt, was das Weglaufen sehr erschwert.  Was das Level Design angeht, wurde bis auf das Hotel, die Stadt bis zur Bar und Teile vom Hospital das Game krass Liniar gemacht, war das Erkunden sehr langweilig und ermüdend gemacht hat. Manche Sachen wurden auch komplett umgeschrieben und ergeben keinen Sinn, wie z.B. das Reparieren der Schallplatte, wozu würde James, der nach seiner Frau sucht sich denken: "Oh ja die werd ich jetzt reparieren und mein Leben dafür riskieren die teile zu suchen"? Es ist einfach unnötig um Spielzeit zu strecken.  Zu dem allem kommt noch das die Kernessenz von der Silent Hill Reihe, die Rätsel, komplett verkackt wurden. Man sieht jetzt an einer durchsichtigen Umrandung, welche Gegenstände man braucht und wo man sie platzieren soll. Und Sachen wie z.B. das Uhrenrätsel keine Gehirnaktivität benötigt, weil man jetzt einfach Raten kann und es so sogar schneller geht. Und andere wie z.B. das Rätsel mit den Gewichten, wo es ganz klar andere Möglichkeiten gibt um die Gewichte richtig zu verteilen, das spiel aber nur eine Möglichkeit als richtig anerkennt.  All in all, eine komplette shitshow, ich würde empfehlen, das Spiel auf leichter Kampfschwierigkeit und schwerer Rätselschwierigkeit zu spielen oder, die weitaus bessere Wahl, es einfach gar nicht erst zu kaufen und sich lieber das Original auf einem Emulator zu spielen.

The grim bleak psychological rollercoaster of Silent Hill 2 feels out of place in 2020s society. It is rather hard, if not downright foolish to try to recreate the feeling of the original game in an exact way. The original story feels edgy, emotional and unconvincing compared to recent narrative horror games, with no common ground to relate to after 24 years. Still it is the one component which Bloober feels they must preserve. You cannot help but recreate the core psychological dilemmas present in the original to tell the same story. But what if these dilemmas do not resonate with modern audience anymore?  The problems are clear:  I) Bloober clearly does not want to tell the story of the main character; this is apparent in all decisions, cutscenes, narrative design, atmosphere, instead it is like they "have to" because they are making a remake. It is like they don't believe in the story themselves, quite weird. II) The original game is quite a generation-specific experience, drawing on the turn-of-the-millennium anxieties creating a bleak world of undisclosed, hidden depravity. None of these foundations exist in the same form in the current society(imo), the world has changed, our thinking and appreciation of stories in video games with it. There could've been some way to preserve the narrative of the original but approach it in much more relatable way.  In conclusion, the remake ends up reconstructing the part of original game which does not "fit into" modern day, the plot, and giving it a modern video game treatment. The result is a game that does not feel genuine, trying to hit the switches which made the original what it was, without translating the plot in a such a way that it would feel gripping in the current age. They innovate in wrong places, changing combat, locations, look and feel of the characters. In the end, it would've been much better if Bloober would've just made a new horror game IP instead, a Silent Hill-like if you will. Then, maybe the result would feel like it actually means something.

Je me demande ce qui est si fameux dans ce remake. Le gameplay : tout pourri. James est raide et lent, ses interactions avec les protagonistes : il ne dit quasiment rien. Les interactions avec les objets  ? il faut appuyer, appuyer... La moitié du temps c'est pour ouvrir des tiroirs vides. on prend des ennemis dans tous les coins. Les dialogues : consternant, James est aux fraises en permanence, il bredouille quelques mots sans signification particulière : il cherche Mary... L’idée de Maria est très bonne mais ça donne quoi ? La DA, c’est moche et dans la pénombre tout le temps. On a l’impression d’un long tunnel glauque. L’exploration, non plus, il y a des ennemis partout et tout le temps et de toutes façons aucun bonus à le faire hormis trouver des polaroids tous pourris. L’histoire : pas mal mais franchement, le jeu en fait quoi d’autre à part punir James à répétition donc le joueur ? Bref c'est une purge pour James et c'est une purge pour le joueur. Le prochain SH ce sera sans moi.  I really don’t get what’s supposed to be so great about this remake. The gameplay? Awful. James is stiff and slow, his interactions with the other characters? He barely says a word. Interacting with objects? Just pressing and pressing… half the time it’s just to open empty drawers. Enemies pop up around every corner. The dialogues? Cringe-worthy. James is completely out of it the whole time, mumbling a few meaningless words: he’s looking for Mary... The idea of Maria is actually good, but what comes out of it? The art direction? Ugly, always drowned in darkness. Feels like you’re stuck in one long, gloomy tunnel. Exploration? Forget it. There are enemies everywhere, all the time, and no real reward for doing it besides finding useless, trashy polaroids. The story? Not bad, but honestly, what does the game actually do with it besides punishing James over and over – and therefore punishing the player? In short, it’s torture for James and torture for the player. The next Silent Hill? Count me out.

I want to start off this review by saying that I have never played the original Silent Hill 2. I don't know if this remake "holds-up" or is as good as the original. With that being said this is one of the greatest horror games ever made, and one of the greatest stories in general. The combat is fun but not too crazy, but at the same time you are kept on your toes. The puzzles are challenging but not too difficult that they become frustrating, and so it is really satisfying to solve them. The graphics are amazing, all the little details around the town, you can tell they really thought this out. The locations are iconic and memorable. The sound design is some of the best I've heard in a video game. Not because it is insanely innovative or anything, but I've never been so afraid in a game solely because of the noises I would hear. There's a part where you're in a dark tunnel and you hear what sounds like giant footsteps clambering towards you. I was in immense panic and kept running out of the tunnel, thinking something was chasing me. But, upon further inspection, it was some kind of creature under the grates on the floor crawling around. All this to say, is that the sound design produced stress, paranoia, and genuine fear into me while playing. The story is really well done. [spoiler] I already had known the big plot twist, but I still was surprised at certain parts and it still is a good game even if you have had it spoiled to you. [/spoiler] Please go into the game as blind as possible. The characters are all interesting as you learn more about them. I will say sometimes the facial animation in cutscenes can feel a little off, but it's not too bad. When you finish the game, you start to see all the symbolism the game uses. (I mean, I didn't understand what the heck was happening), and I highly recommend reading about it online or watching a video about it after playing the game. Silent Hill 2 is one of the best horror games, and video games in general. I wouldn't exactly recommend it at the price it's listed as of writing this review (70$), but if it's on sale definitely grab it. Even if you don't do well with horror games, you should still try it. It doesn't heavily rely on jumpscares, but rather it has building tension and fear through the unknown. Overall an excellent game and well worth your time.

Io dopo aver giocato questo remake posso solo dire che SH2 è un capolavoro senza tempo che con i giusti ritocchi si adatta al gaming di oggi senza perdere niente sia dal punto di vista del gameplay che quello narrativo. Per i più giovani (o anche meno) per favore fatevi un favore, giocatelo senza pensarci due volte perchè al netto dei difetti legati sopratutto ad una ottimizzazione non ottimale (maledetto UE5), Silent Hill 2 è un viaggio nel dolore e nell'affrontare i propri demoni. Di come l'amore possa mischiarsi ad altro e farci fare cose, che per quanto necessarie, possono segnarci in maniera indelebile.

Вот я и прошёл Silent Hill 2 (Remake), и вот моё мнение об этой игре:  🟢 Плюсы Прекраснейший,загадочный и интересный сюжет. If you're not going to take away anything else from this review: [b] Go grab a copy [/b].   SILENT HILL 2 is a stellar game and should be a staple of any modern survival horror enthusiast's catalogue.  The combat feels fluent, responsive and [b]weighty[/b]. The cinematography is amazing. The visuals are beautiful.  The voice acting is great, which I know is a point of contention among fans, but I think it's great.  The story is horrible, visceral, brutal and beautiful. I like to think that SILENT HILL 2's story was meant to be interpreted in different ways, and that's something I won't spoil.   I once saw somebody call the game [i]soulless[/i] and another time heard people say that the game doesn't capture the same magic as the original.  I disagree. If anything, I think the remake improves on the source material, while still staying faithful. It still tells all the same stories, but with the fresh coat of spit, polish and care this classic deserves.

This is a survival horror masterpiece, independent of your appreciation of the original. It has the best of everything that survival horror has to offer, and then some.   The combat is mechanically deep enough to incorporate strategy, and there is a fair bit of it. I like the new combat a lot, the enemies are fast and erratic and James is slow and unsteady. Enemies will scatter and hide in the dark, and ambush you with perfect timing. It's more grounded than games like Resident Evil 4 or Dead Space, but still more action heavy than the original silent hill. Despite the frequency of combat, I still found encounters to be tense and mannequins provided relentless jump scares. The bosses were overall great, and a large improvement to the originals as well.  The puzzles and exploration are what separates this from a lot of other modern, OTS camera style horror games. There are a lot of puzzles, and they are elaborate, multi-step processes that carry over into other rooms, that are usually locked by keys or puzzle sequences linked to other rooms. Nearly every section of the game is like a maze, nothing is ever a straight line and you can never tell what's ahead because it's either too dark, or too foggy.   You're constantly feeling lost while being hunted in the dark, scavenging through run down buildings filled with monsters and dark imagery. The sound design brings it all together, with haunting music and sounds that generally make me want to quit the game. Silent Hill's music has the worst vibes, a symphony of sirens, metal banging on metal, strange distortions, all designed to make you feel bad. It's a perfect horror soundtrack.  It's a pretty long game, 16-20 hours for a first run. Every mechanic gets used to its full potential, there is a lot of combat, a lot of puzzles, and a lot of ground to explore. It remains faithful to the original while providing an even more hardcore experience and more challenging level design. Technical issues aside, it's a must play.

How does someone wipe off their sins when the blood becomes stained, and the perception of your surroundings begin to weigh in? Horror games feel so brushed off in the gaming landscape considering now that most modern catalog of horror games are filled with cheap jumpscares and copy and pasted content. While there have been plenty of good horror games in the past few years, Silent Hill 2 is a reminder of what the standard of horror games should always strive to be. The atmosphere and the environment never makes it feel that you're in one place, one moment could be returning to reality and the next moment you'll be hearing the cries down the hospital hallway. The characters speak so weirdly and although it can be chalked up to be bad voice acting, the voices and out of place characters add so much to how it reflects James and what kind of person he is.   Silent Hill 2 is a must play, even for people who do not like horror games, I can only beg that you try out this masterpiece.

Wife guy horror game (defo not lots of those around).  In all seriousness, amazing game all around.  Level design: this is where the game shines and brings most of its elements together. If you haven't played a Silent Hill game, think of it like a Resident Evil game (closest comparable example I can think of is RE2R). It's a lot about exploring paths and solving puzzles, all while threading through perilous paths and challenging encounters (all heightened by the spooky aspect of the game). Enemy placements never feel unfair (aside from a few challenging encounters towards the end, but they're meant to be hard), but do require situational awareness. Puzzles (and level progress) is always rewarding (it's never too cut and clear but neither too hard, while still requiring some fair brain power for some).  Story and themes: a refined version of the original (imo), and the original is well remembered for a reason. I can't really go into the story itself, but if you haven't played it, there are 2 questions that you should keep in mind: "What is Silent Hill (and its purpose)?" and "Why are the present people here?". It explores deep themes of psychology, while making good use of presentation through gameplay more so than cinematics (which makes it paying attention all the more rewarding, but it isn't the level of interpretation from Soulsborne games if you're worried). There's also some subtle choices the game never makes you aware of that dictate the end of the game (an important aspect is related to a key game mechanic, but it's up to you to guess), instead of having the obvious "choose your ending" options (although if you really don't want to screw yourself over you can always save at the end of the game, as there will be a "choice" before your final confrontation).  Gameplay: as previously mentioned, puzzles and map exploration are great (which is why I urge to not use guides, even when you struggle). The combat is probably the weak point of the game (although this doesn't mean it's bad). Melee never ever really changes throughout the game (you only need to learn a new enemy's attack pattern every so often), and it will most likely be your main recourse as standard enemies are pretty manageable and saving ammo for tough/boss encounters is vital. Gunplay is serviceable (standard third person shooting). However enemies are pretty fun to fight, and the diversity in how they attack you helps making combat fresh for every encounter (accentuated by the level design). Boss fights are also really great (one of which is probably amongst the best in terms of "what makes a good horror game boss fight?"). While your offensive capabilities are "simple" how they are used for which enemies and which scenarios is what makes combat good.  Art direction: one of the best in horror games. The soundtrack and sound design never misses. The world and levels are scary as they are enthralling. The otherworld (and fogworld) are still one of the most unique horror aesthetics conceived. They manage to perfectly capture the feelings of "you shouldn't be here" and "this place shouldn't exist". The environments are filled with gloominess and hopelessness, with shards of hope.  The horror: excellent. The main emotion felt is "uneasy" with certain high tension scenarios. It never goes for the jumpscares, but rather heavily relies on its suspense and slow built-up for the majority of the game, which makes the tense scenarios even more impactful when they do actually happen. The first quarter of the game is mostly used to introduce its world and workings, while the last quarter is where they bump up the horror aspect.

The first Silent Hill I've played and I really enjoyed it. The pulsing stingers that would play during otherwise quiet moments really instilled dread in me any time I thought I was safe. The combat SFX was especially crunchy and I really liked the sound design for all the weapons. If you like the core gameplay of RE games and don't mind something with much less levity I'd check this one out.

First time playing a game from the series so hopefully this review serves as a barometer of sorts for those looking to break into the series. My experience was on a 4080 Super/13700k PC. As many reviews and news outlets have reported, the game suffers from consistent stuttering and hitching which depending on your sensitivity to that will possibly cause you to refund/uninstall or wait out hoping for Bloober to fix it (they won't and they kinda can't to some degree).   At first, I won't lie, it was really annoying to still deal with traversal stutter despite a shader compilation step and adding some mods that supposedly helped to further improve this via a guide here on Steam. I can't say for certain whether they really helped or not. I did not try playing without the mods to see if there was a change. I also did not play at release so it is hard for me to compare my experience to what apparently was an even worse one at launch. As of this time, there hasn't been a patch to the game in several months and like I mentioned above, Bloober will probably not fix this. To some degree, this is a UE5 issue that would require upgrading the engine version used. Newer versions of the engine have apparently added fixes to stuttering/hitching that we've all come to characterize as a fundamental part of playing a game using UE5. From what i've read/heard, this is not exactly easy nor inexpensive to do and so I doubt they will do so especially when they're already working on the remake for the first SH game. On top of that, they're probably also still doling out support for their newer game Chronos: The New Dawn.   To be very clear, I am not excusing this at all. I found it extremely annoying to have lurches while playing despite traversing areas that should have already had all their assets loaded/streamed in the first time. And that is still not acceptable on the first time as well when the shader compilation step is supposed to take care of that. A lot of the games being released now on UE5 all have these issues no matter if its a PC or console version and hence this is something that will only be fixed in time as devs use newer versions of UE5 that have somewhat tackled these engine-level issues. Is it true that devs also have a responsibility here? Definitely. But these recurring issues with UE5 are a problem with the engine itself more so than with developers using UE5.  Anyways, enough of UE5 stuttering issues. The only other visual oddity to me was the game's sort of mixed bag in terms of its presentation. What I mean here is that the game has a habit of both looking good and oddly bad at the same time. There's lots of aliasing, some environments look muddy and of lower quality than other sections in the game, the water was especially bad looking, etc.. Yet, I persisted.  So why did I persist and why am I ultimately recommending this game? Honestly, its because it does horror and atmosphere well which is what I wanted. There's a sort of surreal and dreamy quality as well as goofiness that often reminds me of Twin Peaks which I am huge fan of. There are twists you don't expect and terribly awful things that happen which depending on how you look at them, either help to villanize or endear characters to you. You feel empathy, pity, disgust, bewildered, etc at the various actions they take and their histories which slowly reveal themselves. The game seriously is a slow burn and this is what I hope you take away from the review the most, that if you continue you will be rewarded. I remember thinking about an hour and half in that I was gonna quit cause of the stuttering and the somewhat obtuse map system. The game is also a lot less hand-holdy than other more modern-horror games like the RE remakes.  The puzzles can be a bit confusing but they're definitely more interesting than those I've experienced. The enemies are grotesque, but they are not so oppressive and terrifying in comparison to the atmosphere, sound design, and the environments (despite their somewhat not visually appealing presentation). This is where the horror genre has to excel for me. The tension should be not facing the monsters, but the environment that has allowed them to exist and flourish in.  Again, the BIG TAKEAWAY here is that if you can get over the game's stuttering/mixed presentation is that the rest of the game really takes you on a journey dealing with themes of abuse, trauma, guilt, not belonging, anger, sadness, etc. The game deals with emotions and events that are deeply human and that paint the road to recovery as one marked with many mistakes, backtracking, and even maybe never actually recovering from the ordeal. I played this consistently once I got over my hump and I think that is solely because I wanted to keep going and experience more of the world and the sheer horror. Do yourself a favor,  play the game.

People like to dismiss this game's praise because of how legendary the original is. "The OG is the best horror game ever made, so of course this game is good." That sentiment typically comes from those who haven't played both. In reality, this remake is extremely transformative, taking liberties to rework entire sections of the game, and deeply expand on the story presented in the original. With a game as heavy and as beloved as the original, one wrong addition to the story, one line of dialogue delivered too on the nose, one pause held for just a bit too long, one building that takes just a bit too long to work through, one track remade that strays just a bit too far from the original tone, one gameplay slider tuned a bit too high to make James a little too strong, and the entire experience could've toppled over and been ruined. What's remarkable is, through the vast amount of changes made to the gameplay, the world design, and the story, every single one shows deep understanding and love for the source material, and this remake somehow manages to soar above one of the greatest video games ever made.

У своїх спогадах, я бачу це місто...   Але щось воно не хоче нормально провантажуватись.  Клятий рушій, кінець паршивого хоку.     Як людина що пройшла оригінальну класичну трилогію (найбільше люблю першу частину), намагався грати у четверту частину (мабуть їй теж треба перевидання, бажано таке що доповнює та виправляє оригінал), і забив на всі інші (хоч і знаю що не всі ті ігри повне лайно) я чекав цю гру. Хоч як я вже казав перша частина моя найулюбленіша, і я вважаю що їй перевидання треба куди більше ніж другій, вибір перевидати першою саме SILENT HILL 2 вцілому зрозумілий. Найулюбленіша для більшості частина, та в якій розробники ризикнули та замість піти по сюжету першої гри, натомість вони зробили геть іншу історію де саме місто головний герой, що вершить долі тих кого воно прикликало, показує їм різні проекції себе, та монстрів накликаних їх вчинками з життям. Де від твоїх часто неочевидних рішень впровж гри вирішується, що саме станеться з Джеймсом Сандерлендом вкінці, де та чи інша річ в грі може мати кілька значень, сенсів та інтерпритацій подій. Одним з мудрих речей які зробили конамі (так інколи і в їх голови приходять мудрі рішення, сам в шоці) в цьому перевиданні, було те що вони не віддали робити перевидання невідомій студії чи студії-початківцю як вони це робили впродовж років, чим надовго поховали серію. Натомість вони дали це зробити польській Bloober Team, команді яка вже встигла себе зарекомендувати як творців різних психологічних жахастиків, та які самі були прихильниками SILENT HILL і часто надихались цими іграми під час розробок своїх ігор. Були звісно питання про те як вони зроблять бойову систему, оскільки ні одна з ігор від цих розробників до того не те що не мала боївки, це часто взагалі були симулятори ходьби. Проте знаєте що? Як на мене Bloober Team впоралась що з перенесенням гри, що з атмоферою оригалу, що з бойовою системою, простою як дві копійки проте хочаб зручною, і не такою паскудною як було в усіх трьох оригінальних іграх, та навіть гірше в четвірці. Коли ходиш по місту  то відчуваєш що потрапив саме до Сайлент-Гілу, з його туманом, запустінням і цим клятим тріском радіо коли ти розумієш що вже не сам. Сюжет тут той самий, Джеймс Сандерлент отримує листа від своєї дружини, в якому та запрошує його до Сайлен-Гіллу в їх особливе місце. Всеб нічого, але Мері померла ще 3-ри роки тому він хвороби (гадки не маю якої, цього так і не пояснять) та тим не менш він приїзджає сюди, так наче саме прикликало його сюди... і не тільки його.   Далі не буду вглиблюватись в сюжет, та його головний поворот, хоча як на мене не знати його це те саме, що не знати що Енекін Скайвокер це Дарт Вейдер, Конструктором є Джон Крамер, а в "Психо" весь цей час вбивцею був син який вдягався як вбита ним мати.  Це щось вже давно загальновідоме. Хіба скажу про сюжет ще те, що тепер персонажі не настільки відморожені (крім Еді, він став навіть ще більш відмороженим) а стали більш людяними, особливо Джеймс. Тепер він багато в чому подібний до тих хороших хлопців які слухають, намаються себе вести тактовно, навіть якось допомогти. Жаль звісно, що і таких можна довести до ручки, проте я ніколи не міг його винити в тому що він зробив, і через те що сам був колись в схожій як він ситуації, і через те пекло яке ми пройшли з ним впродовж гри. Проте звіснож не все мені сподобалось. Вигляд персонажів, не тільки Анджели, всі вони вони крім Лаури мені здаються якимись дивними. Джеймс як на мене міг би виглядати більш мужньо чи що, Еді надто вже відморожено та моторошно виглядає, Анджела... так її моглиб зробити більш гарнішою, тай голова Марії таки дійсно велика. Як на мене акторка Мері/Марії більш гарна в реальному житті. Ще я не розумію чого потойбічний світ виглядає як в першій і третій грі, а не як в оригіналі. Він не був в другій частині іржавим пеклом в світлі жовтих ламп, він скоріше виглядав як закинута будівля в яку б ти будучи дитиною чи підлітком на свій страх та ризик міг піти досліджувати. І є момент коли він так виглядає, проте це скоріше спалах з минулого (моменти коли тобі показують той чи інший предмет або місце що були оригіналі але не діють в перевиданні) і все, далі пекло як в першій та третій грі. Проте це так, питання смаку, а от те що оптимізація в цій грі лайно собаче це факт. Цеж знов Unreal Engine 5 шоб його, і так знов вильоти з переглядом діафільму замість плавних кадрів в секунду. Компіляція фейдерів шоб його! Бо не можна ж промальовувати тільки певну частину карти, а решту заховати туманом і плавно показувати по ходу проходження гри, ну не знаю, як в оригінальній першій грі. Ніхто ж про це не знає, цеж не загальновідомий факт так чого в серії з'явився туман, так?  Я навіть порахувати не можу скільки разів в мене вилітала гра, в моменті з першим боєм з Пірамідоговим майже завжди все зависало прямо в відео. Це і стало причиною чого гру я пройшов лиш раз, бо замість того щоб просунутись далі гра зависала, раз за разом, на одному і томуж клятому моменті. Кльова опимізація! Проте... яб всеж порадив зіграти в гру, особливо якщо ви любите оригінал, бо його данину він не паплюжить, проте не забувайте що оптимізація тут лайно собаче.

Ремейк от которого у людей были минимальные ожидания из-за прошлых, довольно слабых, работ студии, но в результате ставший новым золотым стандартом того, как нужно обновлять игры.  [h2] Сюжет [/h2] Сюжет остался таким же, как и в оригинале, за исключением нескольких мелочей и нововведений, но в целом, ничего важного не вырезали, а всё старое воссоздали просто великолепно. Озвучка и мимика в игре очень хорошо сделаны. Оригинал славился тем, что там актёры озвучки не доигрывали, потом в ужасном ремастере новые актёры переигрывали, но тут озвучка реально великолепна. Были изменения дизайнов, которые мне не особо нравятся, но в целом, это скорее вкусовщина и я реально не думаю, что эти изменения вредят. Даже концовки сохранили такими, какие они были.  [h2] Музыка и визуал [/h2] Музыка и визуальная составляющая игры просто великолепны. Что в принципе не удивительно, так-как над этими аспектами ремейка работали те же люди, что и над оригиналом. Каждая локация, каждый монстр, всё сделано великолепно. Очень часто я останавливался и просто удивлялся тому, что игра выглядит как скриншоты в старых журналах с играми, где эти скриншоты были либо из роликов, либо из концепт-артов. У тебя никогда не возникает мыслей по типу "Опять тёмные, серые коридоры", музыка и арт дизайн всегда держат тебя в напряжении. Причём это всё очень явно под влиянием разработчиков оригинала, так-как следующая игра от этих разработчиков даже на 1/10 на столько не впечатляет.  [h2] Геймплей [/h2]  Я думаю, что тут разработчики тоже всё сделали довольно хорошо. Патронов не на столько мало, что бы это раздражало и не на столько много, что бы игрок мог с лёгкостью пробежать, как минимум, на нормальной сложности. Да, когда мы начинаем драться с монстрами и уворачиваться от их атак это выглядит нелепо, но в целом это работает и в разы лучше чем если бы мы вообще не могли драться в ближнем бою. Ещё меня раздражало то, что в некоторых местах лежат враги, которых ты можешь как угодно расстрелять или избить, но как только ты затригиришь их оживление, это всё не будет иметь значения. В целом, это всё мелочи, как и то, что бывает сложно подойти к предмету так, что бы Джеймс с ним взаимодействовал. Я просто рад, что разработчики не попытались сделать ограниченный инвентарь с редкими патронами, как они сделали в своей следующей игре от геймплея которой я плевался.  [h2] Итог [/h2]  Я удивлён. Многие, включая меня, не верили в успех ремейка. Никто не верил, что ремейк будет на столько пропитан любовью к оригиналу. Это то, что я хочу видеть от ремейков. На этом фоне, я ещё меньше стал уважать ремейк RE4, который стыдился оригинала и пытался стать на столько мейнстримным, на сколько возможно. Я надеюсь, что ремейки первой и третьей части Silent Hill не будут уступать по качеству и любви к оригиналу. Это настоящий подарок всем фанатом от явных фанатов.

[h1]Silent Hill 2 Review[/h1]  [h2]TL;DR[/h2] This was my (Meta) first entry in the Silent Hills series, and man - what a masterpiece. It's feels like a perfect middle-ground between Resident Evil and Outlast. First playthrough was 15+ hours and it all felt amazing.  [h3]Gameplay[/h3] [list] [*][b]Combat:[/b] You're not a soldier like in RE games, and you're not a journalist like Outlast. You're a normal guy who can lay pipe.  [*][b]Replayability:[/b] Fairly high. Eight endings and NG+  [*][b]Controls:[/b] Slow, but by design. Entering rooms and rounding corners feels terrifying. [/list]  [h3]Story & World[/h3] [list] [*][b]Premise:[/b] James Sunderland arrives in Silent Hill after receiving a letter from his wife (who’s been dead for years). What follows is a descent into guilt, grief, and psychological torment.  [*][b]Characters:[/b] The characters and enemies are so well done. Every scene with Angela felt so powerful.  [*][b]Worldbuilding:[/b] Silent Hill has life(?) but feels so lonely. Atmosphere pulls you in. [/list]  [h3]Progression[/h3] [list] [*][b]100%-able?:[/b] Yes, and seems to be worth it. Each ending gives you another piece of the puzzle.  [*][b]Leveling:[/b] None, you're really just progressing through James' mind.  [*][b]Gear & Tools:[/b] Flashlight, radio, gun, pipe. Every item matters. [/list]  [h3]Presentation[/h3] [list] [*][b]Visuals:[/b] Everything feels so grotesque and unique. I imagine playing the OG was even better.  [*][b]Audio:[/b] Anxiety inducing and amazing.  [*][b]Performance:[/b] Ran fine until one cutscene, and then I dropped frames to 60fps for stream. [/list]  [h3]Bonus Bits[/h3] [list] [*][b]Mods:[/b] Not sure any are out there, or needed.  [*][b]Multiplayer:[/b] None. Silent Hill is a lonely experience.  [*][b]Steam Deck:[/b] I don't believe it's officially supported, and I don't think you'd get the same experience. [/list]

[h1] ABSOLUTE CINEMA [/h1]  Uzun zamandır denk geldiğim bir oyundu. Korku oyunlarıyla pek aram olmadığından başlamak zor olsa bile oynadığım hiçbir dakikasından pişman değilim. Bloober Team ortaya mükemmel bir REMAKE çıkartmış. Her detayı ve atmosferiyle mükemmel bir REMAKE olmuş.   [h1] Bloober Team - Yapımcı Firma hakkında biraz bilgi [/h1]  Çoğu kişi bu oyunun bu kadar kaliteli olmasını beklemiyordu. Yani Bloober Team'in geçmişine baktığımızda bu gayet normal bir şey ama burada unutulan bir şey var ki o da Bloober Team'in koyu Silent Hill fanı olması. Çalışanlar Silent Hill serisini o kadar fazla seviyor ki kendi yaptıkları oyunlarda Silent Hill'den esinlendiğini görebiliyoruz. Kısacası Silent Hill 2, Bloober Team için sadece bir korku oyunu değildi. Onlar için psikolojik gerilimin ve korku oyunlarının zirvesiydi. O yüzden Silent Hill projesine saygı, büyük bir özen ve detaylara dikkat göstererek yaklaştılar. İşte bu yüzden ben de dahil çoğu oyuncu ters köşe oldu.   [h1] Original vs Remake [/h1]  İlk versiyon 2001 yılında piyasaya sürüldü. Çıktığı dönemden kaynaklı olarak kamera açıları ve ağır mekanikler barındırıyordu. Sabit kamera açıları oyun için gerilimi ve tedirginlik hissini artırıyordu. Kontroller ise günümüze göre daha ağır olduğundan oyun ile uyuyordu. Orijinal versiyonun grafikleri çıktığı dönem için bile etkileyiciydi. Sis, ışık ve gölgelerin kullanımı kusursuz bir atmosfer yaratıyordu. Akiro Yamaoka'nın elinden çıkan ses efektleri ve müzikler de oyunun en güçlü yanlarından birisiydi. Oyun deneyimine unutulmaz bir psikolojik korku ve gerilim ekliyordu.  https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3523985527 REMAKE versiyonunda hikayeye büyük ölçüde sadık kalınmış. Ek olarak karakterlerin geçmiş hikayeleri ve karakterler ile etkileşim geliştirilmiş. Diyaloglar ve olay örgüsü daha anlaşılabilir yapılmış ki bence güzel olmuş. Bu tür geliştirmeler hikayeye dramatik bir ağırlık katıyor. Hala her şey açıklanmış değil ve keşfedilmesi gerekiyor. Bir de belirli sahnelerin ve bölümlerin genişletilmiş olduğunu da unutmayalım. Bu eklemeleri o kadar kusursuz bir şekilde yapmışlar ki sanki orijinal oyundan alınmış gibi duruyor.  Omuz üstü kamerası ve modern aksiyon korku oyunlarına benzer kontrolleri ile oyun daha akıcı bir hale gelmiş. James'in hareketleri daha akıcı olmuş. Bu da keşfi daha eğlenceli bir hale getiriyor. Dövüş mekanikleri bence bir korku oyunu için yeterli hatta yerine göre şaşırtıyor. Saldırılar ve kaçışlar daha hızlı. Kısacası mekaniklerin günümüze az çok uyarlanması daha tatmin edici olmuş.    [h1] Hikaye ve Arka Plan [/h1]  Silent Hill 2'nin hikayesi, ölen eşinden gizemli bir mektup aldıktan sonra Silent Hill kasabasına gelen James Sunderland etrafında dönüyor. Zamanla ana karakterimiz James'in geçmişiyle, vicdanıyla ve içindeki bastırılmış gerçeklerle yüzleştiğini fark ediyoruz. Ek olarak burada biraz yan karakterlerden de bahsetmek istiyorum;  [list]     [*]Angela Orosco, babası ve erkek kardeşi (oe'ler) tarafından tacize uğradığı için travma geçiren genç bir kadın. Silent Hill, fiziksel bir yerden ziyade onun psikolojik acısını yansıtıyor. Hikaye travmanının kalıcı etkisini ortaya koyuyor ve oyuna trajik bir derinlik katıyor. Maalesef üzücü bir geçmişe sahip...      [*]Eddie Dombrowski, zorbalık ve toplumdan dışlanmışlık yüzünden yıkılmış bir adam. İnsanların onunla sürekli alay etmesinden dolayı Eddie, zamanla daha saldırgan ve dengesiz bir hale geliyor. Artan paranoyası ve tehlikeli davranışları, sosyal istismarın zihin üzerindeki yıkıcı etkisini yansıtıyor. Açıkçası kendisini hiç sevmiyorum. Bana çok irite edici geliyor. Sinema'da elini sosun içine sokarak yemesi bile iğrenç bir durumdu.      [*]Maria, tıpkı James'in karısı gibi görünen ama farklı bir kişiliğe sahip bir kadın. James için hem umudu hem de takıntıyı temsil ediyor. James'in bastırılmış arzularını, suçluluk duygusunu ve gerçeklikten kaçışını simgeliyor. James ile olan karmaşık ilişkisi bizleri James'in sorunlu zihninin derinliklerine çekiyor.      [*]Ve son olarak Laura. Hastanede Mary ile gerçek bir bağ kuran saf ve masum bir çocuk. Diğerlerinin aksine Silent Hill onu etkilemiyor çünkü diğerlerini etkileyen suçluluk ve travmalardan yoksun. Hikayede varlığı masumiyeti ve umudu temsil ediyor. [/list]  Silent Hill 2, sıradan bir korku oyunundan çok daha fazlası. İnsan zihninin karmaşık ve kırılgan yapısı hakkında mükemmel bir hikayeye dönüşmüş durumda. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3528549754  [h1] Ses Tasarımı ve Müzik [/h1]  İlk oyunun ses efektlerini ve müziklerini yapan efsane Akira Yamaoka tekrardan REMAKE için işe koyulmuş. Açıkçası Akira Yamaoka'nın müzikleri ve ses efektleri olmasaydı Silent Hill'in aynı olacağını düşünmüyorum. " Theme of Laura " gibi parçalar oyunun duygusal tonunu belirlemekle kalmıyor, aynı zamanda oyunun ruhunu da yakalıyor. Ortamlardaki tüyler ürpertici uğultular, düşmanların boğuk sesleri ve ani sessizlikler tüylerimizi diken diken eden bir atmosfer yaratıyor. Bu inanılmaz ses tasarımı oyunun korkutucu havasının temelini oluşturuyor. Çoğu oyunda olduğu gibi ucuz jumpscare mekaniklerine güvenmek yerine, saf psikolojik gerilim kullanılarak korkuyu derin ve sürükleyici bir hale getiriyorlar. İşte bu yüzden ses tasarımı ve müzikler için efsane.  Ek olarak "Theme of Laura" parçası aynı zamanda oyun tarihinin en ikonik bestelerinden birisi olarak kabul ediliyor.   [h1] Grafikler ve Atmosfer [/h1]  REMAKE versiyon da grafik konusunda oldukça başarılı. Ama burada unutmamamız gereken şey oyunu başarılı kılan sadece grafiksel kalitesi değil, yarattığı kusursuz ve mükemmel atmosfer. Her ortam farklı bir korku ve psikolojik gerilimi yansıtıyor. Sisli sokaklar, paslı hastaneler, nemli odalar ve terk edilmiş otel lobileri, bu ürkütücü atmosfere katkıda bulunuyor. Her bir bölümde ve mekanda çok ince detaylar işlenmiş.   Karanlık koridorlarıyla hapishane bölümü hem fiziksel hem de zihinsel bir boğulma hissi uyandırıyor. Labirent bölümünde düşmanlar bizi kovalarken yaşadığımız panik ve kayıp yön duygusunu mükemmel bir şekilde yansıtmışlar. Çaresizlik hissi aşırı yoğun. Otel bölümlerinde ise geçmişin gölgesiyle yüzleştiğimiz şiirsel bir final bizi bekliyor. Oyun tarihinde böylesine yoğun, baskıcı ve psikolojik olarak uyumlu bir çevre tasarımına çok nadiren rastlanır.   [h1] Oynanış ve Mekanikler [/h1]  Silent Hill 2'nin mekanikleri basit ama tatmin edici bir oynanış sunuyor. Kamera açıları, hareket hissi ve düşman etkileşimleri özenle yeniden tasarlanmış. Saldırılar yerine göre şaşırtıcı derecede tatmin edici. Örneğin bana doğru yaklaşan bir hemşire'nin sol bacağına ateş ettiğimde dizinin üstüne düşüyor ve bir süre öyle kalıyor. Bunun gibi küçük detaylar oyuna ne kadar özen gösterildiğini gösteriyor. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3528155655  [h1] Gerilim ve Korku [/h1]  Silent Hill 2, bildiğimiz jumpscare mekaniğinden uzak duruyor. Bunun yerine, sürekli artan bir baskı, ağır bir atmosfer ve delilik hissi yaratıyor. Psikolojik baskı ve korku hissini oluşturmayı çok iyi başarmışlar.  Unutmayın. Bu oyunda korku sadece bir duygu değil. Bir atmosfer, bir zihniyet ve psikolojik yüktür.   [h1] Düşman Çeşitliliği [/h1]  Oyundaki düşmanlar, alt edilmesi gerekilen hedeflerden çok daha fazlası. Her biri James'in bastırılmış korkularını, duygularını ve suçluluk duygusunu somutlaştırıyor. Biçimleri, saldırı düzenleri ve sesleri kasıtlı olarak rahatsız edici. Elbette bir de Piramit kafa var. James için sadece bir düşman değil aynı zamanda James'in kişisel cezasının da bir simgesi. Sessizliği, tehditkar varlığı ve kaçınılmazlığıyla oyun tarihinin en ikonik figürlerinden birisi haline geldi.   Yukarıda da bahsettiğim gibi düşman tasarımları sıradan korku unsurları olmanın ötesine geçerek hikaye anlatımının ayrılmaz bir parçası haline geliyor. Bloober, ele aldığı esere büyük bir saygı göstermiş. Orijinalin melankolik ruhunu korurken, grafik ve oynanış anlamında günümüz standartları için oldukça iyi hale getirilmiş bir deneyim sunmuş. Oyunun kalbinde, James Sunderland ve uzun, amansız bir hastalıktan muzdarip olan eşi Mary nin yıkıcı hikayesi yatıyor. Mary nin hastalığı ilerledikçe, James in ona olan sevgisi bıkkınlığa, kızgınlığa ve tükenmişliğe dönüşmüştür. James, karısının acısına ve kendi çaresizliğine dayanamayarak, onu duygusal olarak terk etmiş ve acı dolu son günlerinde ondan uzaklaşmıştır. Bu ağır yük ve derin pişmanlık, James in mektup üzerine Silent Hill e çağrılmasının asıl nedenidir. Mektup, James için sadece Mary nin izini sürme daveti değil, aynı zamanda kendi ruhunun derinliklerine gömdüğü gizli bir suçlulukla yüzleşme zorunluluğudur. James in yolculuğu, kısa sürede suçluluk, pişmanlık ve bastırılmış arzularla örülmüş, kişisel bir kabusa dönüşüyor. Bu yolculukta karşılaştığı yardımcı karakterler, kasabanın öznel etkileşiminin en çarpıcı kanıtlarıdır: Maria: James in karşısına çıkan, Mary ye benzeyen ancak çok daha baştan çıkarıcı bir figürdür. Maria, James in cinsel arzu, saplantı ve hayal kırıklığı gibi bastırılmış isteklerinin somutlaşmış halidir. Angela: Kasabanın sisinde kaybolmuş genç bir kadındır. Onun hikayesi, aile içi istismar ve derin çaresizlik temalarına odaklanır. Angela nın gördüğü yaratıklar ve onun bulunduğu ortamlar, kişisel travmasının yarattığı cehennemi yansıtır. Eddie: Genellikle abur cubur yiyen, aşırı kilolu ve beceriksiz bir adamdır. Eddie nin hikayesi ise dışlanmışlık, şiddet ve öfkenin sonuçlarını ele alır. Kasaba, onun bu bastırılmış öfkesini ve intikam arzusunu somutlaştırır. Laura: Kasabada sürekli karşımıza çıkan küçük bir kızdır. Laura, James in gördüğü korkunç yaratıkları ve kaosu görmeyen tek kişidir. O, Mary nin hastaneden tanıdığı ve saf bir bağ kurduğu masumiyeti temsil eder. Laura nın varlığı, kasabanın lanetinin yalnızca günah ve pişmanlık taşıyan yetişkinlerin algısında var olduğunu en güçlü şekilde gösterir. Özellikle Piramit Kafa gibi figürler, yalnızca yaratık olmaktan çıkıp, James in ruhunun derinliklerinden gelen ve onu sürekli cezalandıran suçluluk duygusunun somutlaşmış hali olarak öne çıkıyor.  Tarihin en iyi psikolojik korku hikayelerinden biri belki de en iyisidir. 10/10

Silent Hill 2 - and really the entire franchise - is a unique experience in gaming. When I played the original back in my school years, I felt hopelessness, deep sorrow, and fear. For me, it was the scariest game ever – it didn’t frighten me with jump scares, but with its suffocating atmosphere. Twenty years have passed, and nothing has changed.   The remake crushes you with that same atmosphere from start to finish, carried by the legendary soundtrack of Akira Yamaoka. This is the only game where it feels literally uncomfortable to be there. You want to turn it off, to escape from it - and that is exactly where Bloober succeeded brilliantly.   Yes, there are plenty of excellent survival horrors - Alan Wake 2, Resident Evil 2, 4, 7, 8 - but only in Silent Hill 2 will you feel this. And that’s why the game remains one of a kind.   It’s also unique because of its story - so personal, so intimate for each of its characters: James, Angela, Eddie. If you love narratives rich with psychological depth, this is your game.   And for those who played the original, Bloober prepared surprises: Glimpses of the Past that reference specific moments, scenes, or items from the original game and two completely new endings. Both are worthy of the original, and one of them is so powerful it gives you chills – and you even think, “Yes, this might be the best ending for James.”   An unforgettable game. A unique survival horror. A one-of-a-kind experience that gets under your skin and never lets go.

Silent Hill 2 – Entré buscando a mi esposa y encontré mis traumas 👁️🌫️  Te despertás con una carta de tu esposa… que está muerta. Y como toda persona emocionalmente estable, decidís ir a un pueblo cubierto de niebla, monstruos y pura angustia existencial. Obvio que sí, ¿qué puede salir mal?  Lo bueno:  La ambientación es BRUTAL. Nieblas, calles vacías, edificios oxidados y sonidos que no sabés si vienen del juego o de tus pensamientos más oscuros.  Los enemigos parecen creados por alguien que tuvo 14 pesadillas seguidas. Y funcionan. Son raros, incómodos, y cada uno parece decirte: “esto no es solo un monstruo, es un símbolo emocional, bestie”.  La historia es cortita pero te destruye psicológicamente. Empezás diciendo “ok, quiero saber qué pasó” y terminás llorando en silencio mientras suena un piano triste.  Puzzles. VIEJOS PUZZLES. Pero bien hechos. Te hacen sentir como si resolvieras misterios de tu infancia rota.  Lo malo:  A veces caminás 10 minutos con pura niebla y ruidos horribles… y eso es el punto fuerte.  No te explica nada directamente, tenés que armar todo en tu cabeza (ideal si te gusta pensar… o sobrepensar).  No podés abrazar a nadie en este juego. Y lo necesitás.  Lo mejor:  Los personajes están tan rotos como vos, y eso crea una empatía hermosa y aterradora.  La música. Qué decir. Tristeza, tensión, nostalgia… todo comprimido en un par de notas que se te clavan en el alma.  La sensación constante de que estás siendo castigado… y te lo merecés.
